choices.text: `docker.io/library/alpine:3.22`
choices.why: Right: Docker Hub, the official images' namespace, the repository and the tag.

choices.text: `localhost/alpine:3.22`, the local machine

prompt: An image name with no tag, such as `alpine`, means the tag `___`.
Ana's deployment names `alpine:3.22`. Who decides when the bytes it runs change?
hint: Who can push to the repository?

choices.text: Nobody; a tag with a version number is fixed
choices.why: A tag is a label, and it moves to every new 3.22 build.

choices.text: Ana, because she wrote the version
choices.why: She chose the line; Alpine chooses which build it points at.

choices.text: The publisher, within 3.22
choices.why: Right. Only a digest would leave the decision with Ana.

choices.text: Docker, which updates images every night
choices.why: Docker updates nothing on its own; a pull fetches whatever the tag points at then.

prompt: `docker image inspect` gave the same `Id` for `alpine:3.22` and for its full name. What is that id?

choices.text: A number Docker assigns when it pulls
choices.why: It is computed from the content, so every machine gets the same one.

choices.text: A hash of the name `alpine:3.22`
choices.why: Names do not enter the hash; two names gave the same id.

choices.text: The id of the newest layer only
choices.why: A layer has its own digest; this one names the whole image.

choices.text: The digest of the image's index
choices.why: Right, the same `sha256:5291…` as in `RepoDigests`.

prompt: Match each part of `docker.io/library/alpine:3.22` to what it is.
hint: Left to right: server, account, image, version.

prompt: What did `docker tag shelf:1.0.0 localhost:5000/shelf:1.0.0` do?

choices.text: Gave the same image a second name
choices.why: Right, a name that says which registry to push to.

choices.text: Copied the image, doubling the disk it uses
choices.why: Both names showed the same id; nothing was copied.

choices.text: Sent the image to the registry
choices.why: Sending is `docker push`, which came later.

choices.text: Renamed the image, so `shelf:1.0.0` was gone
choices.why: The listing still showed `shelf:1.0.0`.

prompt: Why did Ana pass the password with `--password-stdin` rather than `-p lab-only`?
hint: Where else would a command-line argument be visible?

choices.text: `-p` is not accepted by `docker login`
choices.why: It is accepted, with a warning about exactly this.

choices.text: So it never lands in shell history or the process list
choices.why: Right. An argument is visible to anyone listing processes.

choices.text: Standard input is encrypted on the way to the registry
choices.why: Encryption on the wire is TLS, whichever way the password was typed.

choices.text: It makes the login last longer
choices.why: How the password is given changes nothing about how long it holds.

prompt: After `docker login`, `~/.docker/config.json` held `"auth": "YW5hOmxhYi1vbmx5"`. How protected is that?

choices.text: Hashed like the htpasswd file, so it cannot be reversed
choices.why: The registry's file is hashed; the client's is merely encoded.

choices.text: Encrypted with a key held by the daemon
choices.why: No key was involved; one command decoded it.

choices.text: Not at all: it decodes to `ana:lab-only`
choices.why: Right, which is what a credential helper is for.

choices.text: Safe, because only Docker reads the file
choices.why: Any program running as Ana can read it.

prompt: The first `docker push` ended in `no basic auth credentials`. How much of the image reached the registry?
hint: What did each layer line say?

choices.text: All layers but the manifest
choices.why: No layer was sent; each one stayed at `Waiting`.

choices.text: The layers it shares with distroless
choices.why: Shared layers would still have to be sent to this registry, which was empty.

choices.text: Half of the layers, which `docker push` resumed later
choices.why: Nothing was sent; the second push sent every layer.

choices.text: None: every layer was still `Waiting`
choices.why: Right; the registry refused before any layer was sent.

prompt: Moving `shelf` from Ana's registry to GitHub's, what changes in the commands?
hint: The protocol is the same everywhere.

choices.text: The address in the name, and how to log in
choices.why: Right; the push and the pull stay as they are.

choices.text: Everything: each registry has its own client
choices.why: `docker push` and `docker pull` work against all of them.

choices.text: Only the tag, which must start with `gh-`
choices.why: There is no such rule; the address is what changes.

choices.text: Nothing; Docker finds the registry by itself
choices.why: The registry is whatever the name says, and the name has to say it.

prompt: Cloud registry logins like ECR's hand `docker login` a password that lasts hours. What does that buy?
hint: Think about the file the password ends up in.

choices.text: Faster pushes, since the token is shorter
choices.why: Speed does not depend on the token.

choices.text: A leaked one is worth little
choices.why: Right: by the time somebody finds it, it has expired.

choices.text: No need for `docker login` at all
choices.why: The token is handed to `docker login`.

choices.text: It lets anonymous users pull without a limit
choices.why: It is about who may push and pull, not about anonymous limits.

prompt: Which of these are the lesson's advice for choosing and running a registry? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Keep it next to where the images run
choices.why: Yes: faster, often free, and no stored password.

choices.text: Give push access to the pipeline and few people
choices.why: Yes: push decides what every server runs next.

choices.text: Set retention rules on the first day
choices.why: Yes: every image is kept and billed until told otherwise.

choices.text: Prefer anonymous pulls from Docker Hub in CI
choices.why: That is what hits the `429` limit.

prompt: Match each image address to its registry.
A deployment must run exactly the image that passed the tests last Tuesday, whatever is pushed since. What should it name?

choices.text: `localhost:5000/shelf:latest`
choices.why: `latest` moves with every push that does not name a tag.

choices.text: `localhost:5000/shelf:1.0.0`
choices.why: A version tag can still be pushed over.

choices.text: `localhost:5000/shelf@sha256:f13b…`
choices.why: Right: the digest is the content, and nobody can move it.

choices.text: `shelf:1.0.0`, without the registry
choices.why: That name means Docker Hub, and still a movable tag.

prompt: A CI runner shared by several projects pushes images. What should a job do about `docker login`?

choices.text: Log in once when the runner is set up, and never again
choices.why: Then every job on the runner holds the credentials, forever.

choices.text: Skip it, and make the registry accept anonymous pushes
choices.why: Then anybody can change what servers run.

choices.text: Pass the password with `-p` so it is not stored
choices.why: `-p` still stores it in `config.json`, and shows it in the process list.

choices.text: Log in with a short-lived token, and log out at the end
choices.why: Right; lesson 26 does exactly that.
